title: Rigveda 10.158: To Surya
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.158: To Surya: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.158 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to Surya. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 138v-139r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.158.1-3 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 16); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 138v
translation.original_text:
1sūryo̍ no di̱vas pā̍tu̱ vāto̍ a̱ntari̍kṣāt | a̱gnir na̱ḥ pārthi̍vebhyaḥ ||
2joṣā̍ savita̱r yasya̍ te̱ hara̍ḥ śa̱taṁ sa̱vām̐ arha̍ti | pā̱hi no̍ di̱dyuta̱ḥ pata̍ntyāḥ ||
3cakṣu̍r no de̱vaḥ sa̍vi̱tā cakṣu̍r na u̱ta parva̍taḥ | cakṣu̍r dhā̱tā da̍dhātu naḥ ||
translation.text:
1MAY Sûrya guard us out of heaven, and Vâta from the firmament, And Agni from terrestrial spots.
2Thou Savitar whose flame deserves hundred libations, be thou pleased: From falling lightning keep us safe.
3May Savitar the God, and may Parvata also give us sight; May the Creator give us sight.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 138v (OPenn image 138, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.157.2 ‹yajñaṁ ca nas tanvaṁ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 139r, begins in RV 10.158.4 ‹-cakṣuṣe cakṣur vikhyai tanūbhyaḥ›. Verses 10.158.1-3 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.158.4-5 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 16); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 139r
translation.original_text:
4cakṣu̍r no dhehi̱ cakṣu̍ṣe̱ cakṣu̍r vi̱khyai ta̱nūbhya̍ḥ | saṁ ce̱daṁ vi ca̍ paśyema ||
5su̱sa̱ṁdṛśa̍ṁ tvā va̱yam prati̍ paśyema sūrya | vi pa̍śyema nṛ̱cakṣa̍saḥ ||
translation.text:
4Give sight unto our eye, give thou our bodies sight that they may see: May we survey, discern this world.
5Thus, Sûrya, may we look on thee, on thee most lovely to behold, See clearly with the eyes of men.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 139r (OPenn image 138, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.158.4 ‹-cakṣuṣe cakṣur vikhyai tanūbhyaḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 139v, begins in RV 10.159.5 ‹-abhibhūvarī›. Verses 10.158.4-5 end on this page; 10.158.4 begins on fol. 138v.
